Likelihood ratio of measured evidence

Source: R/tph.R
preslr.Rd

Weighs measurements (a tissue density, a pXRF calcium level, a marker of antemortem ingestion) under two competing hypotheses, each a normal model of what the measurement would be: the likelihood ratio is the probability of the evidence under H1 over that under H2. Its verbal band follows the usual forensic scale on |log10 LR|: 0 none, up to 1 weak, 2 moderate, 3 moderately strong, 4 strong, 6 very strong, above extremely strong support. The ratio measures support, not the probability that a hypothesis is true.

Usage

preslr(x, m1, s1, m2, s2)

Arguments

x

The measurements: finite numbers.

m1, s1

The mean and standard deviation of a measurement under H1: one number each or one per measurement (s1 positive).

m2, s2

The same under H2.

Value

A list: ll1, ll2 the log-likelihoods, llr their difference (the natural log of the ratio), lr the ratio, l10 its log10, and verbal, the band and the hypothesis it favours.

References

ENFSI (2015). ENFSI Guideline for Evaluative Reporting in Forensic Science, approved version 3.0, 8 March 2015. European Network of Forensic Science Institutes. https://enfsi.eu/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/m1_guideline.pdf

Examples

preslr(c(1.9, 2.3, 2.1), m1 = 2, s1 = 0.3, m2 = 1, s2 = 0.4)
#> $ll1
#> [1] 0.2439917
#> 
#> $ll2
#> [1] -11.60169
#> 
#> $llr
#> [1] 11.84569
#> 
#> $lr
#> [1] 139481.2
#> 
#> $l10
#> [1] 5.144516
#> 
#> $verbal
#> [1] "very strong support for H1"
#>
